channel.title: Eat This guide
channel.description: How Eat This works: ways in, ranking, sources, Mother & baby, accounts and plans.

item.title: Your account
item.description: Sign in with Google to keep favourites, settings and reminder times on every device.

item.title: Access keys
item.description: Make an et_pat_ key for your own script, tick what it may do and when it runs out, show it again within 10 minutes of signing in, replace it with a day's overlap, or remove it.

item.title: The Eat This API
item.description: The Eat This REST API: base URL, the Authorization header, the data envelope, errors, cursor pagination, rate limits, and a curl example for favourites, reminder times, food settings, plan, Family and the food catalogue.

item.title: Connect Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code or Cursor
item.description: Add Eat This's MCP server to Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code or Cursor, choose what the assistant may do, confirm any removal it asks for at /developers/confirm, and disconnect it at once.

item.title: Reminder times in your calendar
item.description: A private calendar address that shows each Eat This reminder time as a daily event in Google Calendar or Apple Calendar, at your region's time, and reaches nothing else in your account.

item.title: Developer changelog
item.description: What changed for scripts, assistants, webhooks and calendar feeds that use Eat This, newest first.

item.title: Eat This for developers
item.description: Use your Eat This favourites, reminder times and food settings from a script, Claude or ChatGPT, your own server or your calendar, on every plan, and what an outside app can never reach.

item.title: Two-step sign-in
item.description: Turn on two-step sign-in for Eat This with an authenticator app, keep ten recovery codes, remember your own browser for 7 days, get back in after losing your phone, and what support can and cannot do.

item.title: Webhooks
item.description: Have Eat This tell your server when a food is saved, a reminder time moves or a plan starts: every event, its payload, Standard Webhooks signature checks in Node and Python, retries, and turning an address off.
